title: Reading files, EOF and stream error indicators
learningObjectives: Use fgetc with an int variable so every byte value and EOF are distinguishable.
Explain why EOF is detected after a read attempt.
Distinguish end-of-file from an input error using feof and ferror.
Check formatted and line-based input return values.
Close streams and handle read and close failures.

understand.concept: fgetc returns int so it can represent every value of an unsigned char plus the distinct EOF indicator. EOF is reported when a read cannot produce another character; feof and ferror then distinguish end-of-file from a stream error. Storing fgetc's result in char can lose this distinction.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct read loops distinguish normal end-of-file from an I/O error and avoid storing EOF in a char before checking it.
understand.analogy: Treat the operation as a clearly specified contract between the program and its data.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's type, lifetime, I/O and object representation rules.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Read one character

Use `int ch = fgetc(file)`. The int type can represent all possible unsigned-char values and EOF. Do not store the result in char before checking EOF.

## 2. Read until EOF

Attempt the read in the loop condition. EOF is discovered by the failed read attempt, not by predicting the end before reading.

## 3. Distinguish conditions

After the loop, use ferror to detect a stream error. If no error occurred, feof indicates that end-of-file was encountered. Do not treat every EOF result as proof of a normal end.

## 4. Other input functions

fgets reads at most one less than the buffer capacity and adds a terminator when successful. fscanf returns the number of successful assignments; check that count before using converted values.

## 5. Close the stream

Check fclose as well. Reading and closing can both report errors, and every successfully opened stream must be closed.

examples.title: Apply the concept safely
examples.code:
#include <stdio.h>
int main(void) { FILE *f = fopen("input.txt", "r"); if (!f) return 1; char line[80]; while (fgets(line, sizeof line, f)) fputs(line, stdout); int failed = ferror(f); if (fclose(f) == EOF) failed = 1; return failed ? 1 : 0; }
